question: Ascent ATK, 5v5, eco round (~1900cr each, pistols/SMG). DEF full-buy. Round start (95s). How do you play this eco to maximize value?

options.label: 5-man rush grouped on one site (A) with flashes, close-range stack and trade to overwhelm the anchor
options.explication_courte: On eco, close-range grouping plus flashes plus trades can overwhelm an isolated anchor; even if you lose the round, you may grab rifles and reset the economy.

options.label: Discipline save: take 1-2 safe long-range picks and bank the credits for a full-buy next round
options.explication_courte: The light-save (safe picks then save credits) guarantees a full-buy next round; defensible if the score makes a conservative round correct.

sources_option.citation: A disciplined save takes safe long-range picks and preserves credits for a guaranteed next-round buy, trading round-win chance for economy stability.

options.label: Spread 5 solos across the whole map to take 5 individual duels and fish for frags everywhere
options.explication_courte: Spreading on eco removes your only advantage (close-range numbers): each solo duel against a rifle at any distance is a losing trade.

sources_option.citation: Grouping up to hit one site lets you set crossfires and trade; scattering into individual duels wastes the numbers advantage an eco relies on.

options.label: Force-buy: spend ~1900cr on Spectres/armor for everyone and play like a normal round
options.explication_courte: Force-buying at ~1900cr breaks the economy: you cannot buy correctly OR save, and you end up in a partial buy limbo next round too.

sources_option.citation: Forcing a weak half-buy on a low economy leaves you underequipped this round and broke the next; commit to a proper eco or save instead.

explication_longue:
Situation: Ascent ATK, 5v5, eco round (~1900cr per player, pistols/SMG), DEF full-buy, round start (95s). Maximize eco value without breaking the economy.

Eco principle: the single advantage you have is close-range numbers. On eco, the 5-man grouped rush on one site is the highest-EV play: get close, use flashes, trade - at point-blank range, pistols compete with rifles. Even losing the round is acceptable if you grab rifles along the way.

The discipline save (acceptable) guarantees a clean full-buy next round and is correct when the score makes conservative play right. Spreading 5 solos (costly) is the classic eco mistake: every 1v1 at range against a rifle is losing. Force-buying at ~1900cr (mistake) traps the team in a partial buy limbo with no clear path to full-buy.

Estimated elite distribution: ~52% grouped 5-man rush, ~25% discipline save, ~16% spread solos (costly), ~5% force-buy (mistake).

sources.citation: Group up and hit one bombsite together to set crossfires and trade; absolute coordination with flashes and immediate trades wins eco rounds.
Rushing a site with grouped pistols and flashes can overwhelm an off-position defender, or a disciplined save preserves the economy.
On eco, prioritize teamwork and positioning to outmaneuver better-equipped adversaries; don't force a broken half-buy on a low bank.

_gaps.incertitude: Rush (optimal) vs save (acceptable) depend fortement du score et de l'etat d'economie de la manche : a certains scores, le save discipline devient optimal. Le contexte de manche exact n'est pas fixe par l'enonce (seuil ~1900cr donne).
Estimations depuis guides eco (mobalytics, theguide, allvalorant) ; pas de dataset sur la frequence rush vs save a ~1900cr par elo en elite.
Positions x/y approximatives sur A Main Ascent (viewBox 1000x1000, zones maps.ts) ; le site cible du rush (A) est un choix read-dependent partiellement isole dans l'enonce.
